note: Character arcs for rivals (Examples §7 A-D). An arc is assigned at birth from personality, style or path, turns after the first fight (or 3 stages), and resolves after 3 fights (or 8 stages): well if the rival is empathetic and resilient, badly otherwise. The arcs about Pokémon bonds and Overdrive wait for those systems.

arcs.resolution: Learns to respect preparation, collaboration, and opponents.
Develops a style that fits their own strengths.
Learns to adapt rather than endlessly repeat the same routine.
Builds a reliable support network without losing independence.
Learns to value the relationship behind the performance.
Finds a new reason to compete—or chooses a different life.

arcs.beginning: Doesn't want the responsibilities of success.
arcs.resolution: Decides what kind of Champion they actually want to become.
Achieves success through patience and self-knowledge.

arcs.beginning: Copies the player's team and techniques.
arcs.resolution: Develops an independent identity and may surpass their inspiration.

arcs.beginning: Defines success around beating one opponent.
arcs.resolution: Learns to pursue personal goals—or becomes consumed by obsession.

arcs.beginning: Loses status after a major defeat.
arcs.resolution: Rebuilds honestly or resorts to desperate shortcuts.

arcs.beginning: Lives under a famous predecessor's reputation.
arcs.resolution: Establishes their own legacy or remains trapped in comparison.

arcs.beginning: A betrayal damages a central relationship.
arcs.resolution: Reconciliation, permanent separation, or a new understanding.
Learns restraint or suffers increasingly serious setbacks.
Confronts the insecurity driving the behavior.

arcs.beginning: Justifies unfair tactics to keep up.
arcs.resolution: Takes responsibility, hides the truth, or doubles down.
Learns to respect individual needs—or embraces an increasingly ruthless approach.
Rebuilds their principles or decides that winning matters more than fairness.
Healthy competition, resentment, or reconciliation.
Cooperation, friendship, or an alliance that remains competitive.

arcs.beginning: Another trainer competes for the same person, goal, or title.
arcs.resolution: A three-way rivalry, alliance, or change in priorities.

arcs.beginning: A respected mentor loses faith in the rival.
arcs.resolution: Earned reconciliation or independence from the mentor's expectations.

arcs.beginning: Wants to change how the League operates.
arcs.resolution: Wins institutional influence, compromises their ideals, or becomes disillusioned.
Takes responsibility for another trainer, community, or team.
Returns with a different philosophy or never comes back.

arcs.beginning: Gradually becomes stronger and more independent.
arcs.resolution: Forces the player to respond, accepts a new relationship, or moves on.

arcs.beginning: A major conflict is never properly resolved.
arcs.resolution: Reopens later, possibly in another region or during a world event.
